Vitamin E is the most important of those contained in coconut, providing its antioxidant capacities. It also contains vitamin C, and to a lesser extent type B1 and B2 vitamins. It must be taken into account, as we will see later, that it has a great caloric power.
COCONUT IS A NATURAL SOURCE OF FIBER

Due to the calories coconut contains and its amounts of water, it is an ideal fruit for making energy drinks, juices and sports preparations or energy waters. In this way, minerals such as potassium or sodium can be used. For all these reasons, coconut is the perfect ally to combine with other fruits in juices or drinks.
Cosmetic opportunities are also part of the properties of the coconut, which has become one of the most used fruits to make moisturizers, oils, purifying waters and hair solutions.

The persimmon is a high-energy food, which thanks to its sweetness offers a nice flavour and it is easy to consume. Its contributions include from vitamins to fibre or even carbohydrates.

The persimmon is rich in vitamin C, essential element in the improvement and strenghtening of our immune system; also in betacarotene or provitamine A, giving the persimmon antioxidant properties.

The mango fruit is an exotic food very appreciated in cooking due to all its different possibilities. We are talking about a juicy and refreshing fruit ideal for having in summer in the shape of mango fruit concentrate, among other possibilities.
This tropical fruit provides us with great quantities of vitamin C and pro vitamin A, being an important booster of our immune system. Moreover, the mango fruit has many carbohydrates, so it is perfect for athletes.
It contains water in a high percentage of its weight. In fact, in some cases, the mango fruit water reaches to complete the total volume of its weight (75%-80%) Because of this it is considered to be very refreshing and moisturizing.
THE MANGO FRUIT PROVIDES ANTIOXIDANTS

Among the minerals complementing the mango fruit, we find a remarkable quantity of potassium and magnesium. The first one is very useful to erase the wastes of cells, while the other helps attaching the calcium in bones.

The mango fruit has a satiating power and, due to its fibre, is a natural laxative, being advisable in weight-loss diets. Other fruit with a high fibre volume are the tangerine, raspberry and the pineapple.

The watermelon is a sweet fruit which inevitably, because of its freshness and taste, reminds us to the summer. Rich in vitamin C and vitamin A, the watermelon is good to our body in many different ways.
The vitamin A is an important source of beta-carotene, helping to protect the sight and the skin; on the other hand, the vitamin is beneficial to reinforce our immune system, among other things.
In the watermelon, the beta-carotene it is strenghten by the action of lycopene. This combination turns the watermelon into a very healthy food, which linked to vitamin c, helps to prevent cardiovascular diseases and possible cancerous conditions.
THE 92% OF WATERMELON’S WEIGHT IS WATER

Thanks to this high water volume, the watermelon has a diuretic effect and helps to remove unnecessary substances from our body. Furthermore, It is a versatile fruit to be eaten, both in juices or purees, as well as seasoning dishes.

The watermelon has high levels of potassium, a mineral which adds control to the blood pressure and helps to improve the cardiovascular system. Something similar to what is offered by the banana and the pear.
The watermelon is a high healthy food that can be consumed in juices, concentrates or purees.
